author: Pallas, 1776

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가며, 번식지에서는 6월경 알을 낳는다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 우리나라를 지나가는 드문 나그네새로 여겨진다. 물가 갈대밭이나 숲속에 몸을 숨겨 좀처럼 모습을 드러내지 않으며, 주로 딱정벌레, 메뚜기, 벌 따위 곤충을 먹는다. 시베리아 남부, 몽골 북부, 만주, 아무르, 우수리 등지에서 번식하는데, 물가 풀밭이나 관목 숲의 0.3~1.5m 높이 나뭇가지 위에 둥지를 짓고 알을 4~6개 낳는다. 중국 남부, 인도 아삼~네팔, 말레이반도 등지에서 겨울을 나고, 우리나라와 중국 동부 등지를 지나간다.

points.en: ear coverts paler than the back
dark horn upper mandible, pale brown lower mandible

similar.how: 몸 크기가 비슷하다(원문은 다른 점을 적지 않았다).

art.subject: Thick-billed Warbler (Arundinax aedon), adult (sexes alike) in autumn: crown, back and scapulars plain, slightly rusty olive-brown; rump and uppertail coverts warmer rufous-brown; face strikingly plain: yellowish-white lores and a narrow pale eye-ring, with no supercilium and no eye-stripe; ear coverts paler than the back with faint pale shaft streaks; chin, throat and lower breast buffy-white; upper breast and flanks olive-buff; wings plain brown with rufous-brown edges; tail long, graduated, plain rufous-brown; short, deep bill with a dark horn-brown upper mandible and pale brown lower mandible tinged yellow at tip and base; brown iris; lead-grey legs.
art.pose: skulking low in reeds near water, partly hidden
art.scene: Korean autumn riverside reed bed with scattered shrubs; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched in reeds: plain rusty olive-brown upperparts, plain face with yellowish-white lores and eye-ring and no supercilium, ear coverts paler than the back, buffy-white throat and lower breast, olive-buff upper breast and flanks, long graduated tail
adult, head and bill close-up in profile: short, deep bill with a dark horn upper mandible and pale brown lower mandible tinged yellow, pale lores, plain face with a beady dark eye
art.build: Large warbler, about 18cm, about the length of Oriental Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus orientalis) and much longer than a sparrow, with a heavy body, rounded head and long, rounded (graduated) tail. Bill short for so large a warbler, deep-based and stout with a curved culmen, clearly shorter than the head. Legs strong, grey. Short, rounded wings: at rest the primaries project only a little beyond the tertials. Skulks low in dense reeds and shrubs.
avoid: Do not paint a pale supercilium or dark eye-stripe — that is Oriental Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus orientalis); the Thick-billed Warbler has a plain face.
Do not paint a long, thin bill; it is short and deep.
Do not paint streaks on the back or breast.
Do not paint a short square tail; it is long and graduated.
